Summary (auto): simulated incident dry-run revealed ambiguity in runbook steps 4-6, KV cache eviction timing and quantization skew cause transient error rates, fallback selected a lower-capacity model variant which increased latency more than expected.
Topics detected: kv cache, quant skew, canary throttles, runbook gaps, observability holes

[00:00] Olivia: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, this is the launch failsafe sprint retro and simulated incident debrief, we ran the simulation yesterday at 02:30 and wanted to scrub what we saw and lock owners, so gonna go around quickly for observations
[00:18] Marcus: yep, really quick context, this was a scheduled sim, scope was staged kv eviction followed by a synthetic load that changes seq length distribution to cause quant-path divergence, we were testing fallback routing to ded- vs hosted variants, the canary should have throttled earlier but it didnt
[00:36] Samir: yeah and small note, our canary throttle is based on token error rate with a 5 minute window, by the time it crossed threshold the fallback had already routed half the traffic to the smaller model, so latency spiked
[00:54] Nina: is the issue then metric latency, or metric selection, like are we watching the wrong thing?
[01:05] Alex: i think it is both, the error signal we used is model token failures, which is noisy with quant skew, and the latency delta is what users feel, but we only trigger on the failure signal, not the latency slope
[01:22] Priya: plus the kv eviction was aggressive in the sim, the sim used a ttl of 30s which maybe wasnt realistic, but it helped surface the weak spot in kv reclaim timings
[01:36] Olivia: right the runbook step 4 says "confirm kv reclaim" but doesnt say how to measure, who owns it, or what thresholds mean proceed/abort, that was one of the ambiguous bits we flagged
[01:54] Marcus: what happened operationally, did handoffs work? I saw paging get routed to a dev list rather than SRE oncall for a short window
[02:05] Samir: yeah that was my bad, i misread the oncall rotation in the doc, the playbook references the old rotation name, so escalation route failed and it delayed human intervention by ~8 minutes
[02:21] Nina: 8 minutes is...a lot when latency is 2-3x but good grab. we should probably fix the doc and maybe add an automated paging step for certain metric thresholds
[02:38] Leah: i started a dashboard PR but i want to add two more synthetic checks: prefix cache hit rate, kv eviction delta, and a seq-length spike detector. i'll link the pr in slack after the call (link: https://redwood.app/ops/dashboards/PR-2345)
[02:55] Daniel: the runtime behavior was interesting, the quant path between float16->int8 had a mismatch for longer sequences, so token probability drifts, that produced more sampling failures and triggered our failure metric earlier than we expected
[03:14] Marcus: is this runtime issue per-model or architecture? i.e. can we bake a per-model quant profile or is it a kernel selection bug?
[03:26] Daniel: initial repro suggests it's sensitive to sequence length distribution, it's reproducible across the transformer family we onboarded, so probably kernel selection / quant pipeline needs tighter per-model profiles, also the kernel fallback sometimes picks a slow path that ends up costing more tokens = higher cost but also higher latency
[03:45] Samir: we've seen that before, the kernel selection rules prefer stability, but in fallback it picks a compatibility kernel that doesnt use the optimized attention path, so perf penalty is higher than expected
[04:02] Alex: and that ties back to our routing rules, when capacity is tight the router picks a compatible variant, but we didnt enforce a latency ceiling on that choice, so the router thought "compatible = ok" but product users saw 2x latencies
[04:21] Olivia: action: add a latency ceiling for fallback routing decisions; Marcus can you own approval of that threshold?
[04:31] Marcus: yes ill take it but want Leah and Alex to propose the concrete numbers, we need to balance cost vs user impact
[04:42] Priya: i want to call out runbook clarity again—during the sim the first step for SRE said "if prefix cache < X, then evict", but we dont have a consistent X across clusters, some clusters use percent, others absolute keys, that ambiguity made metric triggers inconsistent
[05:03] Nina: agreed and product side also needs a clearer tolerance matrix — how much quality drop is acceptable during a launch failing scenario? we need a documented drop budget
[05:19] Marcus: we have an SLO budget but it's per-service, not per-route. Perhaps we need per-route launch budgets for sensitive routes (chat flows, embeddings for search)
[05:34] Samir: i also want to mention the canary timeline, it's currently 30m warm-up + 60m observe, the sim only ran for 20m because we had constraints, so we didn't fully exercise the long tail effects
[05:52] Olivia: note to self: for the next sim extend to 90m if possible, but we also need a smaller fast sim that reproduces critical behaviors for quick checks
[06:05] Alex: re: observability gaps, the traces didnt capture kernel selection metadata in the model-level spans, we need to add the chosen kernel id and quant profile to the span tags so we can correlate with latency & token errors
[06:20] Leah: yep im adding kernel_id and quant_profile to span schema. small caveat, adding span tags will increase trace cardinality so we must be careful about our ingestion budget
[06:32] Marcus: maybe we add a sample-rate for kernel telemetry and keep full telemetry for failing traces only
[06:40] Samir: question: what about fallback to hosted variants? yesterday the router picked a hosted variant in eu-west and that added network hop latency, is hosted fallback acceptable in a launch?
[06:53] Nina: product perspective: hosted fallback is ok for non-latency-critical routes but for live chat we prefer degraded model on same infra to avoid cross-region hops, we should make that explicit in the routing policy
[07:08] Olivia: agreed, add a routing policy table: route type -> allowed fallback set (same infra/local variants, hosted, or degrade to cached responses). Samir add this to the checklist
[07:19] Samir: will do, i'll add a routing matrix and the owner field in the checklist
[07:25] Priya: there was one weird transcription in the sim logs that i want to bring up — the kv cache eviction actually happened but the eviction notifications didnt reach the routing layer due to a short wire bug; it's a telemetry publish race
[07:40] Daniel: we saw a spike in publish latencies to the control-plane event bus at the same time, it looks like backpressure on the bus due to a storming client, need to investigate whether the client was the sim harness or a real job
[07:56] Leah: follow-up: i'll add a synthetic test that intentionally storms the pubsub with 500 events/sec for 10s to ensure the event bus has graceful degradation
[08:07] Olivia: ok let's jot down the high priority fixes and owners, low priority can be triaged into the sprint backlog
[08:16] Marcus: high priority: clear runbook ambiguity (owner & thresholds), latency ceiling on fallback routing, add kernel_id/quant_profile telemetry, fix oncall rotation doc and automated paging
[08:31] Samir: medium: create routing matrix and stress tests for event bus, adjust canary timing and launch sim duration

[10:16] Olivia: perfect. quick recap of next steps and owners (read aloud): Marcus approve latency ceiling, Leah dashboard PR + synthetic checks, Samir bench + routing matrix, Alex update canary playbook & paging, Priya stress script, Olivia finalize runbook, Nina prep customer Q&A
